name: alert-dialog
description: A modal overlay that requires an explicit user decision before the page can continue. Use when both confirm and cancel are real choices, not when cancel is simply 'close the modal'.

notes: Footer button fills are set by the parent alert-dialog on button instance roots — this is intentional Figma composition, not an R8 violation.
Destructive type icon-container uses color/status/danger-subtle fill — icon inside may use color/status/danger-subtle/foreground (valid paired-surface).

changelog.change: Destructive stories (Destructive, DestructiveCentered): confirm button switched from asChild + <Button variant='destructive'> to AlertDialogAction className={buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' })} (shadcn-canonical). The asChild approach made Radix Slot concatenate AlertDialogAction's default buttonVariants() (primary) with the child's destructive classes without tailwind-merge, so primary won and the confirm rendered blue. Story-only; component tsx unchanged.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.
darkMode.pairedSurfaceRisk: icon-container Destructive uses color/status/danger-subtle — icon must use danger-subtle/foreground, not color/icon/danger.

notes: No × close button on destructive modals — closing ≠ cancelling. If × is needed, use Dialog instead.
Focus is trapped by Radix on open. Initial focus goes to first focusable element (cancel button).
Backdrop click does NOT close — by design. Forces explicit decision.

AlertDialogAction already applies buttonVariants() (default primary). For a destructive confirm, pass className={buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' })} on AlertDialogAction. Do NOT wrap a nested <Button variant='destructive'> via asChild — Radix Slot concatenates both classNames without tailwind-merge, so primary wins and the button renders blue.

relatedComponents.name: alert
relatedComponents.reason: Alert is inline non-blocking; AlertDialog is modal and blocks until decided

relatedComponents.name: dialog
relatedComponents.reason: Dialog has neutral close (×/backdrop); AlertDialog forces an explicit decision

relatedComponents.name: button
relatedComponents.reason: Footer buttons are Button instances — Primary or Destructive for confirm, Outline for cancel

blocksWhen: open === true — blocks all page interaction

alert-dialog.purpose: Overlay modal requiring explicit user decision — Align × Footer × Type

intent.Left: Default layout — title and description left-aligned. Use for longer explanatory text.
intent.Center: Centered layout — use for brief, unambiguous confirmations with short title.

intent.Inline: Buttons side by side, right-aligned. Use on desktop with short button labels.
intent.Full-width: Buttons stacked, each full width. Use on mobile or when labels are long.

intent.Default: Non-destructive decision — acknowledgement, confirmation, terms. Cancel may be equivalent to ×.
intent.Destructive: Irreversible or high-stakes action. No × allowed. Both buttons are real decisions.

composition.alignment: LEFT or CENTER per Align variant
rules: Footer buttons are Button instances — set via Variant prop, never repaint internally
Backdrop click does not close — Radix default for AlertDialog
No × button on destructive type — both buttons must be real decisions

animation.description: Overlay fades in. Panel zooms in from center (zoom-in-95). Reverses on close.

liveRegion.announces: dialog title and content on open — role=alertdialog triggers assertion

keyboard.Escape: Close dialog, return focus to trigger

accessibility.touchTarget: Buttons meet 44px minimum via Button component

storybook.title: Overlay/AlertDialog
storybook.notes: Footer gap fixed 2026-06-03: flex-col gap changed from xs (4px) to sm (8px) per spec. Destructive confirm uses buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' }) on AlertDialogAction (not asChild + nested Button) — verified red in light + dark 2026-06-17.

usage: Use only when the user must make a decision before continuing.
Both confirm and cancel must be real choices — not just 'close the modal'.
Type=Destructive: always include a cancel path with clear labeling ('Cancel', 'Keep my account').
doNot: Do not add a × close button to Type=Destructive — closing ≠ cancelling.
Do not use for non-blocking feedback — use inline alert instead.
Do not use for forms or complex content — use Dialog instead.
Do not override button fills inside footer button instances — change Variant prop instead.
Do not use generic 'Are you sure?' — describe the specific consequence.

forbidden: AlertDialog with form fields (use Dialog instead)

useCases: Confirming workspace or project deletion — irreversible, user must explicitly choose
Revoking admin access for a team member — high-stakes, affirmative choice required
Discarding unsaved changes — 'Save' or 'Discard' are both real decisions
Accepting terms of service before accessing a restricted area
Confirming a subscription charge or payment before it processes
Overwriting an existing file — both 'Overwrite' and 'Cancel' are meaningful

Type=Default.whenToUse: Decision required but not destructive — acknowledgement, confirmation, opt-in

Type=Destructive.whenToUse: Irreversible or high-stakes action where confirm is dangerous

Footer=Full-width.whenToUse: Long button labels or mobile layout
examples: 'Yes, delete my account' / 'No, keep my account' stacked

Align=Center.whenToUse: Brief, unambiguous confirmation with short title and description

comparedTo.situation: Feedback that doesn't block the user
User can close without deciding (× is a valid exit)
Complex form or multi-step flow in a modal
